chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When blood or something else comes out from the nostril of the deceased after the washing and hits the turban or the shroud, cut it off with the cutter.
ai.seo_question: What should be done if blood stains the shroud of the deceased after ritual washing?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses a specific nuance in the ritual washing (ghusl) of the deceased, noting that impurities like blood may emerge post-washing, thereby requiring the cutting (qarad) of the affected area of the shroud or turban to maintain ritual purity. It highlights the practical rigor of Shia fiqh in ensuring the sanctity of the burial attire, reflecting the scholarly attention to minute details of taharah. The ruling underscores the principle that the state of purity must be preserved until the moment of burial, even if minor impurities appear after the initial washing process.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abdullah Bin Yahya Al Kahily, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the blood comes out from a nostril of the deceased, or something (else) after the washing and hits the turban or the shroud, cut if off with the cutter’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kahiliy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If anything comes out of the nostrils of a deceased, like blood and so on, after Ghusl (bath) and such things come in contact with turban or shroud, such parts (of shroud) must be cut off and disposed.’”
